flashcards.back: No. Only the ignorant think them different; mastering one brings the benefit of both.
True renunciation is hard to reach without Karma-yoga; a sage with Karma-yoga quickly attains God.
One who neither desires nor hates, free of the pairs of opposites. Renunciation is inside, not outside.
The yogi acts through body, senses and mind, knowing nature moves them, not the Self.
One who offers all work to the Lord, without attachment, is untouched by sin, as water never wets a lotus leaf.
To purify the mind: they act with body, mind and intellect, but without attachment.
Giving up attachment to fruits brings supreme bliss; attachment to them binds.
The body. The Self dwells in it as its master, neither acting nor making others act.

flashcards.front: Does God create our doership or our Karma?
flashcards.back: No. Nature does; God takes neither anyone's sin nor merit. Ignorance veils this.
The enlightened see the Lord in all: a learned priest, an outcast, a cow, an elephant, a dog.
They come from contact, begin and end, and are wombs of pain. The wise don't delight in them.
Unattached to sense pleasures, one finds the joy of the Self through contemplation and enjoys spiritual bliss.
One who can withstand the force of desire and anger before leaving the body.
Those merged in the Source, devoted to it as goal and refuge, their impurities removed by its knowledge, are not born again.
Senses outside shut out, gaze steady, breath even, free of desire, fear and anger: knowing God, they reach peace.

quiz.text: Who thinks renunciation and Karma-yoga are different?
quiz.why: 5.4: master one and you get the fruit of both.

quiz.text: Why is Karma-yoga called the more accessible path?

options.A: Renunciation is hard to attain without it

quiz.why: 5.6: with Karma-yoga a sage quickly reaches God.

options.D: Inner freedom from desire and hate

quiz.text: What image shows freedom from sin in 5.10?

options.B: A tortoise drawing in its limbs

quiz.why: Work offered to the Lord leaves no stain, like water on a lotus leaf.

quiz.text: What is the "city of nine gates"?
quiz.why: The Self dwells in the body as its master.

quiz.text: Who creates our sense of doership and Karma?
quiz.why: God is not the author of Karma; nature operates through beings.

quiz.text: What does the enlightened see in a priest, an outcast and a dog?
quiz.why: 5.18: equal vision, the mark of wisdom.

quiz.text: Pleasures born of sense contact are:

options.C: Sources of pain with a beginning and end

quiz.why: So the wise find happiness within.

quiz.text: Which two forces must be mastered before leaving the body?
quiz.why: Who withstands them is a yogi and a happy person.
